title: Centered global ring maps satisfy the coefficient order lower bound
statement: Let $N$ be an affine scheme, $b\in N$, $m,n,s\in\mathbf N$, $\alpha:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to\mathbf N^n$ any exponents and $c_{i\gamma}\in\Gamma(N,\mathcal O_N)$. Let $T:\Gamma(N,\mathcal O_N)\to\kappa(b)[[W_1,\ldots,W_m]]$ be a ring map whose constant coefficient is residue evaluation at $b$. Form the family $f_i$ and the germ-defined locus $S(\alpha,c)$ of [def-trf-coefficient-division-data]. If $b\in S(\alpha,c)$, then $|\alpha_i|\le\operatorname{ord}(f_i)$ for every $i$, where zero has infinite order. No smoothness, etaleness, characteristic or first-exponent assumption is imposed.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.

proof.text: The affine stalk is the localization of global sections at the point prime. A denominator has unit germ, hence nonzero residue. Its image under T has unit constant coefficient and is a unit. Extend T to the stalk by IsLocalization.lift. Constant coefficient of the extension equals the residue homomorphism by localization uniqueness.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.

proof.text: For each p, the series of order at least p form an ideal J_p. The inequalities for orders of sums and products show J_r J_t <= J_(r+t), hence J_1^p <= J_p by induction. The stalk extension maps the maximal ideal into J_1 and thus its p-th power into J_p.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.

proof.text: Split an exponent into its W and Z components; their degrees sum to its total degree. For total degree below d_i, the order-locus hypothesis and the preceding power-ideal bound force its Taylor coefficient to vanish. MvPowerSeries.nat_le_order gives the result.
